earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists (Radlinski 1892, Krasheninnikov 1755, Volodin 2021 dictionary); no grammar/phonology of extinct Northeast Itelmen found.

sources.citation: Bobaljik, Jonathan David, Maria Pupynina & Arzhaana Syuryun (eds.). 2023. Bogoras's 1901 Itelmen Notebooks / Ительменские тетради В. Богораза 1901. Vol. 1 -- Texts (Studies in Linguistic Anthropology). Fürstenberg/Havel: Kulturstiftung Sibirien & СПбФ АРАН
sources.note: Editors' introduction: Bogoras's diacritics 'include an acute accent for stress'; Bogoras and Jochelson 'consistently mark stress on the full vowel following an excrescent vowel' (e.g. -kazú-); these are remarks on Western Itelmen transcription, not a stress rule, and nothing concerns the Eastern language. 39 MB file searched in the work dir and not.

sources.citation: Халоймова, К. Н., М. Дюрр, Э. Кастен, С. Лонгинов. 2012. Историко-этнографическое учебное пособие по ительменскому языку (Языки и культуры народов Дальнего Востока России; Ительменский язык и культура т. 1). Fürstenberg/Havel: Kulturstiftung Sibirien, 164 pp. (1st ed. Kamshat, Petropavlovsk-Kamchatskij 1995/1997); language material of the Mil'kovo 'Kamchadals' collected by the club «Камчадалы»
sources.note: In the 'Фонетика' primer section on the glottal stop sign: a syllable closed by the glottal stop always carries the stress, although in Itelmen stress is basically on the first syllable. Stated for modern Western Itelmen; must not be attributed to east2812.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for east2812 (Northeast Itelmen; alt. East Itelmen; status extinct) with its two references: Georg & Volodin 1999 pp. 216-224 and Worth 1961 pp. 595-596 (both tagged subclassification)
sources.note: Bibliographic only; Glottolog lists no grammar, phonology or sketch for this languoid.

sources.citation: [unsigned]. n.d. (c. 2022-2025). Itel'menskij jazyk [The Itelmen language]. In: Interaktivnyj atlas korennyx malochislennyx narodov Severa, Sibiri i Dal'nego Vostoka Rossijskoj Federacii: jazyki i kul'tury. Moskva: Institut jazykoznanija RAN (atlaskmns.ru).
sources.note: Extinct by c. 1900 per the page; words only; no prosody. No statement.

sources.citation: [unsigned]. n.d. (c. 2022-2025). Восточно- и южнокамчадальский языки [The Eastern and Southern Kamchadal languages]. In: Интерактивный атлас коренных малочисленных народов Севера, Сибири и Дальнего Востока Российской Федерации: языки и культуры (web atlas, atlaskmns.ru; Russian and English versions). Sections: I Социолингвистические данные; II Лингвистические данные (1 classification, 2 диалектная ситуация, 3 история изучения, 4 'Основные лингвистические сведения (фонетика, грамматика, лексика)' with a 50-item Western/Eastern/Southern comparative table after Мудрак 2008, 5 'Яркие лингвистические характеристики'); III Иллюстративные материалы; краткая библиография (18 items); архивные материалы.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No prosody anywhere. §II.4 says outright that nothing beyond word lists survives: «К сожалению, поскольку мы не имеем текстовых материалов на вымерших восточно- и южнокамчадальском языках и вынуждены довольствоваться лишь списками лексики, мы не можем делать выводов о грамматическом устройстве этих языков и их отличиях от западнокамчадальского.» and §III: «по южно- и восточнокамчадальскому языкам не существует текстовых материалов, так же отсутствуют аудио- и видеозаписи. Единственные доступные языковые материалы – списки лексики». Its 'phonetics' content is a 50-word West/East/South table ta…

sources.citation: Володин, А. П. (главный составитель); Оно, Ч. (ред.). 2021. Полный ительменско-русский словарь. СПб. / Fürstenberg/Havel: Kulturstiftung Sibirien (Studies in Linguistic Anthropology). Section «Восточноительменско-русский словарь», pp. 353-359, plus preface pp. 11-12 on the three Itelmen languages and their sources
sources.note: Nothing: the Eastern section is a short list of forms taken from Dybowski (Дыб_В) and Krasheninnikov (Крш_В) with no stress marks; the word 'ударение' does not occur in the file. Preface: Eastern Itelmen disappeared 'в конце XIX – начале XX вв.'; Dybowski 'застал в живых ещё все три ительменских языка'; Tyushov (1890s) found the Eastern language 'только у весьма немногих людей преклонного возраста'.

sources.citation: Institut jazykoznanija RAN, Laboratorija issledovanija i soxranenija malyx jazykov. 2019-2026. Itel'menskij jazyk. In: Malye jazyki Rossii (web encyclopedia, minlang.iling-ran.ru).
sources.note: Mentioned only historically (extinct; voiced stops); no prosody. No statement.

sources.citation: Dürr, Michael. 2013. Die Erforschung der Sprachen Kamčatkas. In: Erich Kasten (Hg.), Reisen an den Rand des Russischen Reiches: Die wissenschaftliche Erschließung der nordpazifischen Küstengebiete im 18. und 19. Jahrhundert, 287-296. Fürstenberg/Havel: Kulturstiftung Sibirien (electronic edition)
sources.note: Nothing on accent. It quotes Erman's remark on the 'abgekürzten und unbestimmten Klang der Vokale in den Vorschlags- und End-Silben' (1848: 435-438) as an observation on transcription difficulty and dialectal/allophonic variation, and notes Steller's use of 'Sonderzeichen und Diakritika' to render Itelmen words; no statement of where stress falls in any variety.

sources.citation: Mudrak, Oleg A. 2008. Kamchukchee and Eskimo glottochronology and some Altaic etymologies found in the Swadesh list. In: Aspects of Comparative Linguistics (Аспекты компаративистики) 3. Moscow: RSUH Publishers, pp. 297-336
sources.note: no phonology content for Itelmen; classificatory remark only (p. 297)

sources.citation: [IEA RAN]. c. 2005. Itel'menskij jazyk. In: Jazyki narodov Sibiri, naxodjashchiesja pod ugrozoj ischeznovenija [Endangered languages of the peoples of Siberia] (web survey, Institut etnologii i antropologii RAN, lingsib.iea.ras.ru).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology; no statement.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A., P. Mühlhäusler & D. T. Tryon (eds.). 1996. Atlas of Languages of Intercultural Communication in the Pacific, Asia, and the Americas (Trends in Linguistics. Documentation 13). Berlin/New York: Mouton de Gruyter. DOI 10.1515/9783110819724. [held page-text, 1903 PDF pages]
sources.note: No phonology. Krasheninnikov regarded the 'eastern language' as the 'standard' Itelmen; Krasheninnikov and Dybowski-Radlinski materials support 'three closely related languages' rather than three dialects; the eastern language's 'last speakers died in the twenties and thirties of the 20th century'; Uka river basin as Itelmen-Koryak contact zone at the northern border of the eastern group.

sources.citation: Jarceva, V. N. (gl. red.). 1990. Lingvisticheskij enciklopedicheskij slovar'. Moskva: Sovetskaja enciklopedija. Entries: Krejnovich, E. A. 'Omokskij jazyk'; Volodin, A. P. 'Itel'menskij jazyk'; [unsigned] 'Jukagiro-chuvanskie jazyki' (online transcription tapemark.narod.ru/les).
sources.note: No statement.

sources.citation: Стебницкий, С. Н. 1934. Ительменский язык. In: Языки и письменность народов Севера, ч. III (Палеоазиатские языки), pp. 85-104 (§13 Ударение, p. 89)
sources.note: §13 p. 89: «Ударение в ительменском так же как в луораветланском и нымыланском, падает на начало слова, чаще всего на первый или второй слог.» — this concerns the Western dialects (Khairyuzovo, Sedanka, Sopochnoe) only; Eastern Itelmen is not treated (Dybowski's southern data are cited once for a plural suffix).

sources.citation: Ditmar, Karl von. 1900. Reisen und Aufenthalt in Kamtschatka in den Jahren 1851-1855. Zweiter Teil: Allgemeines über Kamtschatka. St. Petersburg (Beiträge zur Kenntniss des Russischen Reiches). New edition: Michael Dürr (Hg.) 2011, Fürstenberg/Havel: Kulturstiftung Sibirien (Bibliotheca Kamtschatica), 263 pp.
sources.note: no phonology content; only language vitality c. 1853: in Koraki..Kamaka 'fast kein kamtschadalisches Wort mehr', in Kirganik..Jelofka 'Diese Sprache existiert noch, jedoch sehr verunstaltet, wie die Kamtschadalen selbst eingestehen' (ed. p. 191)

sources.citation: Radliński, Ignacy. 1891. Słowniki narzeczy ludów kamczackich. II. Słownik narzecza Kamczadałów, zamieszkałych nad rzeką Kamczatką, ze zbiorów Prof. B. Dybowskiego. Kraków: Akademia Umiejętności (offprint from Rozprawy Wydziału Filologicznego AU t. XVI, pp. [130]-[217]; 88 pp.)
sources.note: Nothing. Pure alphabetical wordlist (Dybowski 1879-83, Cyrillic originals in parentheses, Latin transliteration, Polish/Latin glosses, Krasheninnikov forms marked 'Kr.'). page scan checked: the Cyrillic forms carry no accent marks; no words 'akcent/przycisk' anywhere in the 90-page text.

sources.citation: Erman, Adolph. 1848. Reise um die Erde durch Nord-Asien und die beiden Oceane in den Jahren 1828, 1829 und 1830. Erste Abtheilung: Historischer Bericht, Dritter Band. Berlin: G. Reimer. XX. Abschnitt (September 1829), pp. 426-447: 'Einige Proben von der Sprache der Kamtschadalen des Kamtschatkathales' -- words heard at Maschura and Jelowka (Kamchatka River valley) set beside Erman's own Sedanka list and Krasheninnikov's 1755 columns a/b/c, numerals, two 'Kamtschadalische Reden' re-transliterated from Steller/Krasheninnikov, and remarks on pronunciation (pp. 437-439)
sources.note: No stress rule is stated. Two first-hand phonetic remarks: (p. 437-438) 'auch verwischen sich beim Sprechen noch viele, in den geschriebenen Worten stark hervortretende, Unterschiede durch den abgekürzten und unbestimmten Klang der Vokale in den Vorschlag- und End-Silben der Worte, und durch den eigentümlich zischenden Laut mit welchem die Consonantenverbindungen in den letzteren begleitet werden' [many distinctions are blurred in speech by the shortened, indistinct quality of the vowels in the initial (pre-) and final syllables of words, and by the peculiar hissing that accompanies consonant…

sources.citation: Klaproth, Julius. 1823. Asia polyglotta. Paris: A. Schubart. xvi+384 pp. (+ folio Sprachatlas). Ch. XIV 'Kamčadalen', pp. 321-322 (introduction and Deutsch-Kamčadalisch comparisons; the Kamchadal word lists by locality are in the Sprachatlas, pp. XXXXIX ff.). archive.org item asiapolyglotta00klap (Princeton Theological Seminary copy).
sources.note: Nothing. The Kamchadal chapter says only that the inhabitants call themselves Itülmen/Itelmän, border the Koryak in the north, that their language 'theilt sich in vier Hauptdialekte' with Koryak admixture near the border (the 'Korjaken am Tigil' being of Kamchadal stock), and refers the compiler to the Sprachatlas for the vocabularies; then two pages of etymological look-alikes with Turkic, Persian, Ossetic, Samoyed, Germanic etc. A a full-text search for stress/accent the whole 839 KB scanned for Betonung/Accent/Ton/Aussprache finds no passage about Kamchadal. Silent pointer; the Sprachatlas…

sources.citation: Сарычев, Гавриил А. 1811. Путешествие капитана Биллингса чрез Чукотскую землю от Берингова пролива до Нижнеколымского острога, и плавание капитана Галла на судне Черном Орле по Северовосточному океану в 1791 году; с приложением словаря двенадцати наречий диких народов [..]. Санктпетербург: Морская типография. Appendix 'Краткий словарь двенадцати наречий разных народов, обитающих в северовосточной части Сибири и на Алеутских островах.. собран бывшим при Экспедиции капитана Биллингса штаб-лекарем.. Робеком' [Michael Robeck/Rohbeck], Отделение III 'Наречия Камчадалов: Большерецких, Камчатки реки [title page: Нижнекамчатских], Тигильских', slovar' pp. 111-121. (Russian original of the lists printed in Latin script in Sarytschew's German edition, Bd. 3, Leipzig 1815: 141-175; CIHM microfiche no. 18629, on archive.org.)
sources.note: Bare three-column Russian-glossed word list (c. 110 entries: God, kin terms, body parts, then nature terms, numerals etc.) in pre-reform Cyrillic. page scan of slovar' pp. 111-112 (pp. 135-136) checked: the Kamchadal forms carry NO accent marks (unlike Krasheninnikov 1755's list) and Отделение III has no remark on pronunciation; the appendix's only phonetic footnote («Буква Ю съ черточкою должно произносить, какъ француское u») sits in an earlier section. Wordlist-only data, no statement; scanned text and a extracted text extract of pp. 135-146 kept beside the PDF.

sources.citation: Sauer, Martin. 1802. An account of a geographical and astronomical expedition to the northern parts of Russia.. performed.. by Commodore Joseph Billings, in the years 1785, &c. to 1794. London: T. Cadell, jun. & W. Davies. Appendix I 'Vocabulary of the Yukagir, Yakut, and Tungoose (or Lamut) languages'; Appendix II 'Vocabulary of the languages of Kamtshatka, the Aleutan Islands, and of Kadiak'.
sources.note: No statement; no marks.

sources.citation: Lesseps, Jean-Baptiste-Barthelemy de. 1790. Travels in Kamtschatka, during the years 1787 and 1788. Translated from the French [Journal historique du voyage de M. de Lesseps, Paris 1790]. 2 vols. London: J. Johnson. Vol. 2, pp. 383-403 'Vocabulary of the Kamtschadale, Koriac, Tchouktchi, and Lamout languages'; pp. 404 ff. 'Vocabulary of the Kamtschadale language at St. Peter and St. Pauls, and at Paratounka'; vol. 1, p. 146 'Idiom' (Bolcheretsk) and Preface (pronunciation of the transcription).
sources.note: No remark specific to the eastern/Kamchatka-river Kamchadals; the only prosodic-sounding remark in the book concerns Chukchi vs Koryak ('a habit of prolonging the final syllables of words, and a pronunciation slower and sweeter', vol. 2 line 725-727), not Itelmen.

sources.citation: Dürr, Michael. [n.d., held as ]. Paper on the early lexical sources for Itelmen (Steller 1774, Krasheninnikov 1755, Ditmar, Dybowski) and Itelmen ethnobiological vocabulary
sources.note: Nothing on stress or on Eastern Itelmen; discusses Steller's and Krasheninnikov's wordlists as sources for vocabulary only (a full-text search for stress/accent eastern/Radliński/Dybowski/Betonung/Akzent: no hits).

sources.citation: Steller, Georg Wilhelm. 1774. Beschreibung von dem Lande Kamtschatka, dessen Einwohnern, deren Sitten, Nahmen, Lebensart und verschiedenen Gewohnheiten. Frankfurt/Leipzig: Fleischer. New edition: Erich Kasten & Michael Dürr (Hg.) 2013, Fürstenberg/Havel: Kulturstiftung Sibirien (Bibliotheca Kamtschatica), 280 pp. Language passage = edition pp. 19-21 [orig. pp. 9-12]; Koryak glossary pp. 234ff; Eastern ('Nischna', 'Nischna-Schandalsky') plant and animal names passim
sources.note: Only an impressionistic characterisation (edition p. 21 [orig. 12]): 'Was den Unterschied der Sprache, ihrer Aussprache nach, anbelangt, so bleibt die itelmenische halb in dem Hals und Mund stecken.. wird leise und mit vielen Ziehen, Dehnen und Torturen, auch wunderlichen Gebärden ausgesprochen' (the source of Krasheninnikov's 'половиною в горле.. с протяжением' already held by the project). Dialect division with the Kamchatka-River language singled out (p. 19-20). Eastern lexical items carry macron/breve (length/prominence) marks but there is no statement about accent. No phonology section.

sources.citation: Крашенинников, С. П. 1755. Описание земли Камчатки, т. 2. СПб.: Императорская Академия наук. Part 3, ch. 1 (on the peoples' languages) and the chapter «О различных наречиях Камчатского народа», pp. 138-142 (wordlist, column A = 'наречие северных Камчадалов' = Kamchatka River = Eastern Itelmen)
sources.note: No statement of a stress rule. The only remark on pronunciation: «Камчатской язык выговаривается половиною в горле, и половиною во рту. Произношение их языка тихо, трудно, с протяжением..». BUT the printed wordlist carries acute accent marks on the Kamchadal words (checked visually pp. 138-140): in column A (Eastern) the mark is on the first syllable in most items (Ку́тъ 'god', Ка́на, Ко́галъ 'sky', Та́тгажъ, Ше́мтъ 'earth', Чи́депечь 'daughter', То́но 'hand') and on a later syllable in a fair number (Корѣ́лъ 'snow', Гале́нъ-кулечь 'sun', Еже́нгынъ 'star', Куну́кулечкуй, Пыну́жидычь, Кея́га '…
